subject: hans_johnson_1904

shot.build: DEV PREVIEW · dev@0e85be38 · Nov 6, 2026, 1:38 AM CT

silhouette.what: Silhouette and fit of the clothes
silhouette.note: Long dark box coat to below the knees, stand collar and buttons read as the role at both distances. At 3 m the coat's body still follows his chest, upper arms and waist; Rau 1902 and Griffith 1905 show a heavy wool coat standing off the body, square at the shoulder and full at the chest.

folds.note: The skirt hangs past the box in a few long folds as in Rau 1902. The lap shows none of the heavy gathered folds where the photographed coats bunch over the thighs and at the elbows.

hat_hair.note: Tall silk hat with a curled brim, set level, hair dark below it: the same silhouette as all three pictures at 3 m and 10 m. The hat throws no shadow on his face (see skin).

skin.note: At 3 m the face is one smooth even tone with no shadow under the hat brim; the photographed faces are modelled, shaded under the brim and darker at the jaw. Phone at Balanced shows the face softer still.

hands.note: Bare hands held apart with open palms. Griffith 1905 shows white gloves and Penfield pale gloves, and all three gather reins (and Rau a whip) in a closed hand at the lap. No whip.

stance.what: How the figure stands or sits
stance.note: Upright on the box with knees high and boots on the footboard, as Rau 1902 and Penfield show; at 10 m he reads as a dark upright block above the team, as Griffith 1905's coachmen do.

motion.note: Five frames over 5 s of his own time at 3 m: small breathing and gaze changes, no jerks or pops. No photograph can show motion; judge it on dev.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever laid the stills beside the pictures; each checklist item is {what, status, note} with status open | reads | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling — open when a visitor would see the figure is not the pictures’ kind of person in that respect. The first figure of each role is the owner’s call (the plan’s "Your call"); later figures of the role are held to the one he approved. A reshoot of a changed figure (bound) sets the verdict back to unreviewed.
